title: Step Functions state machine and durable orchestration
summary: State transitions, branching, parallel work, wait and failure paths form explicit execution history; application data stays downstream.

title: Step Functions optimized and AWS SDK integrations
summary: Optimized integration patterns have service-specific contracts; AWS SDK integration calls supported operations with task-role IAM permissions.

title: Workflow initiation and caller permissions
summary: Caller permissions to start, inspect and stop executions differ from the state-machine execution role used for downstream tasks.

title: Task, Wait, Choice, Parallel and Map states
summary: Task invokes work; Wait delays; Choice branches; Parallel runs branches; Map iterates with concurrency and failure controls.

title: Standard versus Express execution contracts
summary: Standard runs up to one year with durable execution; Express runs up to five minutes; synchronous and asynchronous Express delivery differ.

title: Retries, Catch and terminal workflow outcomes
summary: Retry uses matching error names, interval, backoff and maximum attempts; Catch routes exhausted failure; Fail and Succeed terminate.

title: Human approval and callback task token
summary: Callback task token waits for external approval or job, with SendTaskSuccess/Failure and heartbeat/timeout controls.

title: SQS decoupling and write buffering
summary: A durable queue absorbs producer spikes and lets consumers scale independently while monitoring backlog and age.

title: SQS standard delivery and idempotent consumers
summary: Standard delivery is at least once with best-effort order; deduplicate business effects and recover safely after a crash.

title: SQS FIFO message groups and deduplication
summary: FIFO ordering is per message group; deduplication window and message deduplication ID do not replace consumer idempotency.

title: SQS receive, visibility, delete and long polling
summary: Receive hides a message for visibility timeout; successful worker deletes it; long polling reduces empty receives.

title: SQS retention, delay and payload boundaries
summary: Queue retention, delivery delay, visibility and payload maxima govern recovery and scheduling; use S3 pointer for larger payloads.

title: SQS DLQ and redrive controls
summary: DLQ redrive policy and maxReceiveCount isolate poison messages; fix cause, inspect metadata, then redrive deliberately.

title: Lambda SQS event source mapping and partial batch response
summary: Lambda polls SQS in batches, scales by event-source mapping settings, and can report individual failed item identifiers.

title: SQS backlog capacity and operational signals
summary: Approximate visible/in-flight counts and oldest age reveal backlog; tune consumer capacity and alarms for throughput.

title: Request and response through separate queues
summary: Two queues support asynchronous requests and replies with correlation ID, expiration, deduplication and independent workers.

title: Amazon MQ broker migration fit
summary: Amazon MQ runs ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ; IBM MQ/TIBCO clients require migration or adapter work and operational testing.

title: SNS publication and independent subscribers
summary: Publish once to an SNS topic; each subscription receives independently according to its endpoint protocol and policy.

title: SNS subscription filters and payload routing
summary: Subscription filters can inspect message attributes or body, with delivery and propagation caveats.

title: SNS direct publish, mobile push and service sources
summary: SNS Publish can target topics or eligible endpoints; mobile push uses platform application and endpoint via APNs/FCM.

title: SNS encryption, IAM and topic policy
summary: Topic IAM/resource policy, KMS key grants and destination queue policy jointly control encrypted cross-account fanout.

title: SNS to SQS durable fanout
summary: SNS fans out to separate durable SQS queues; each subscriber retries and consumes at its own pace.

title: S3 event fanout and SNS versus EventBridge
summary: S3 notifications can target SNS for simple fanout or EventBridge for event-pattern routing to more target types.

title: SNS to Firehose delivery path
summary: SNS subscription to Firehose delivers selected publications through delivery role, buffering and destination controls.

title: SNS FIFO topic and subscriber semantics
summary: SNS FIFO orders by message group for eligible subscriptions; SQS FIFO or standard endpoints have distinct behavior.

title: EventBridge buses and event pattern routing
summary: EventBridge default/custom/partner buses and event patterns route matching events to rules and targets.

title: EventBridge target delivery retries and DLQ
summary: Rule target retry and SQS DLQ address failed target delivery; target API acceptance does not prove handler success.

title: EventBridge cross-account bus policies
summary: Event bus resource policy authorizes cross-account PutEvents; source IAM and target rule role govern later delivery.

title: EventBridge archive and replay
summary: Archive captures matching events for chosen retention; replay re-enters bus and can re-trigger rules.

title: EventBridge schema registry and versions
summary: Schema discovery and versioned bindings help typed consumers, while producers/consumers own compatibility.

title: EventBridge Scheduler for cron and one-time schedules
summary: Scheduler supports one-time, rate or cron schedules, time zones, flexible windows, execution role, retry and DLQ.

title: EventBridge Pipes source, filter, enrichment, target
summary: Pipes polls supported sources through optional filter and enrichment to a target; checkpoint/retry depend on source.

title: Choreography versus orchestration
summary: EventBridge choreography routes independent reactions; Step Functions orchestrates bounded business processes and compensation.

title: Messaging choice matrix across SQS, SNS, EventBridge and MQ
summary: Select queue, topic, event bus or broker by delivery, ordering, replay, retention, policy and migration contract.

title: Walkthrough: poison message to DLQ and redrive
summary: Create source queue, DLQ and worker; trigger bounded failures, inspect receive count, fix, redrive and clean up.

title: Walkthrough: SNS to two SQS subscribers
summary: Create SNS topic and two SQS subscribers with policies and filters; publish prod/dev/test, verify and clean up.

title: Walkthrough: workflow retry and compensation
summary: Run Standard workflow with bounded Retry and Catch; inspect execution history, compensation and cleanup.

title: Walkthrough: EventBridge pattern and failed target
summary: Use matching and nonmatching events; inspect failed API Destination delivery, retry record, DLQ and permissions.
